item.title: PNG-US disaster exercise tests emergency response skills
item.description: Disaster response teams in Lae have tested their skills in a joint Papua New Guinea-US exercise focused on saving lives during emergencies. The four-day exercise brought together PNG agencies and the Wisconsin National Guard to train in search and rescue, medical response and site security.
item.content:encoded:
Disaster response teams in Lae have tested their skills in a joint Papua New Guinea-US exercise focused on saving lives during emergencies.

The four-day exercise brought together PNG agencies and the Wisconsin National Guard to train in search and rescue, medical response and site security.

Teams demonstrated how casualties could be removed from disaster areas, treated by medical teams and moved through a secure site.

James Kenwolf, from the US Center for Excellence in Disaster Management and Humanitarian Assistance, said the training was also about strengthening regional security.

“Disaster preparedness is the ultimate expression of our shared commitment to regional security,” Kenwolf said.

The exercise followed a crawl, walk and run approach, allowing trainees to build their skills before taking part in the final field demonstration.

Training also included oil spill response at the Port of Lae, search and rescue, medical emergencies and managing displaced people.

The exercise is aimed at improving coordination between PNG and US agencies and strengthening PNG’s capacity to respond to future disasters.

item.title: K70m district hospital to transform healthcare in Usino
item.description: A new K70 million Level Four district hospital is set to be constructed at Walium in the Usino local level government [LLG] area, bringing major relief to thousands of rural villagers in Madang. The health facility was announced by Usino-Bundi MP Vincent Kumura during a official visit to the district headquarters at Walium last week.
item.content:encoded:
A new K70 million Level Four district hospital is set to be constructed at Walium in the Usino local level government [LLG] area, bringing major relief to thousands of rural villagers in Madang.

The health facility was announced by Usino-Bundi MP Vincent Kumura during a official visit to the district headquarters at Walium last week.

Kumura said the health project is part of a multi-million kina development package planned to upgrade basic services across the district.

The Level Four hospital is expected to significantly improve frontline medical care, reduce costly travel to Madang town for specialized treatment, and cater to the growing population of Usino-Bundi.

Kumura said the project anchors a broader health and community welfare initiative, which includes a K12 million Water, Sanitation and Hygiene [WASH] project currently being rolled out starting at Ramu Sugar, a solar energy project for Gusap, and a K2 million community development center jointly funded with the Department of Community Development, Youth and Religion.

Kumura reassured the locals that he was committed to continuing and elevating the work initiated by his predecessor.

"I want to clear some questions once and for all," Kumura told the crowd.

"I came to keep the light burning, to retrace the footsteps of Jimmy Uguro (late MP), to continue the works he started. I did not come to spoil his work. I came to move his works to another level, and I want you to understand this."

Kumura revealed that his administration inherited an empty District Development Authority [DDA] account, K250,000 in the operating account, and an outstanding K1.2 million tax debt owed to the Internal Revenue Commission [IRC] when taking office following last year's by-election.

He confirmed that the IRC debt has since been fully settled, allowing the district to move forward with major capital works.

He urged people across Usino, Bundi, and Gama LLGs to remain united and support transparent governance.

"Speak one voice only, united Usino, Bundi, Gama. Distribute services equally depending on the size, length, and breadth of our LLGs," Kumura said.

"However, based on the principles of good governance, I will not support previous works that have no reports from the district administration because public funds belong to the people."

Kumura expressed gratitude to government line agencies, corporate partners including Ramu NiCo Limited, and development stakeholders for supporting Usino-Bundi's development agenda.

item.title: Farmers relieved after downpour
item.description: Relief has finally come for subsistence farmers in parts of Simbu province after rainfall ended a 14-week dry season. Downpour was recorded in Chuave, Gumine, parts of Sinesine-Yongomugl, Kundiawa-Gembogl and Kerowagi districts.
item.content:encoded:
Relief has finally come for subsistence farmers in parts of Simbu province after rainfall ended a 14-week dry season.

Downpour was recorded in Chuave, Gumine, parts of Sinesine-Yongomugl, Kundiawa-Gembogl and Kerowagi districts.

NBC News understands it rained for several hours on Sunday, Monday, Tuesday and Wednesday this week.

Farmers in the affected areas said their withered food crops had begun to recover following the downpours.

In Kundiawa, the Simbu provincial capital, an estimated two-hour rainfall was recorded on Sunday afternoon and Monday night, with about 50-minute shower on Tuesday evening.

Meanwhile, local leaders in Karimui-Nomane are calling on the District Development Authority to fund immediate drought relief supplies after communities were affected over the last two months.

Salt local level government president Bolkiabo Goroba and Kilau ward member James Gulabe said they had written to Karimui-Nomane MP Francis Yori and the DDA requesting rice, flour and other food supplies for mass distribution in remote communities.

The duo said the DDA should divert funds from infrastructure projects to drought relief, after the prolonged dry season devastated gardens across the district.

“We are appealing to MP Yori and the DDA to prioritize our people’s food security,” Mr Goroba and Mr Gulabe said in a joint statement.

Attempts to reach MP Francis Yori for comments were unsuccessful.

Karimui-Nomane district administrator Gabriel Kaupa said the national government had not allocated any funding for drought relief operations in the district.

With the rainy season now starting, farmers are hopeful that consistent rainfall will help restore food gardens that were badly affected by the drought.

item.title: Unitech expansion puts pressure on campus infrastructure
item.description: The Papua New Guinea University of Technology is expanding its engineering programmes. But the university says its infrastructure must grow with it.
item.content:encoded:
The Papua New Guinea University of Technology is expanding its engineering programmes.

But the university says its infrastructure must grow with it.

Vice-Chancellor Professor Ora Renagi raised the concern during the launch of the new School of Petroleum Engineering in Lae.

The school will take its first Bachelor of Petroleum Engineering with Honours students in 2027.

Renagi said the programme was a direct response to the growing demand for skilled engineers in the petroleum and energy sectors.

However, introducing new programmes and increasing student numbers will put pressure on the university's existing facilities.

More student accommodation will be needed.

So will classrooms, laboratories, staff housing and other support facilities.

"Growth in academic programmes and student numbers must be met by investment in infrastructure," Renagi said.

The Petroleum Engineering programme is part of a wider expansion at Unitech.

The university plans to introduce Aerospace Engineering and Computer Engineering in 2027.

Railway and tunnelling courses are also planned under Civil Engineering.

Agricultural Mechanisation is expected to follow.

Renagi said the programmes were designed to meet the changing skills needs of the country.

But, the university cannot deliver that expansion without support from government and industry.

He is calling on the government, mining and petroleum industries to work with Unitech on infrastructure development.

Renagi pointed to the earlier partnership between government and the mining industry that helped establish the Mining Engineering School.

He said the same approach could be used to support the new Petroleum Engineering School.

The Vice-Chancellor has also made a direct appeal to Prime Minister James Marape to consider transferring the Telecom College facilities to Unitech.

He said the facilities could help the university manage its expansion and increase its capacity to train skilled workers.

Unitech is also looking beyond Papua New Guinea.

The university wants to attract students from the Pacific and Asia through its internationally accredited engineering programmes.

Renagi said the university's ambition was to become globally competitive while continuing to produce engineers who can contribute to Papua New Guinea's development.

But as more programmes come on stream, the pressure is now shifting from what Unitech can teach to whether it has enough space and facilities to teach them.

item.title: Plans for national nickel hub revealed by Kumul Minerals
item.description: Kumul Minerals Holdings Limited is planning a national nickel hub in Madang province as part of a wider strategy to process more of Papua New Guinea’s minerals domestically, instead of exporting partially processed products. Kumul Mineral Holdings Managing Director, Sarimu Kanu outlined the proposal during a question-and-answer session with Business Advantage International Publishing Director Andr
item.content:encoded:
Kumul Minerals Holdings Limited is planning a national nickel hub in Madang province as part of a wider strategy to process more of Papua New Guinea’s minerals domestically, instead of exporting partially processed products.

Kumul Mineral Holdings Managing Director, Sarimu Kanu outlined the proposal during a question-and-answer session with Business Advantage International Publishing Director Andrew Wilkins at the Business Advantage PNG Investment Conference in Brisbane on Tuesday.

Kanu said the proposed hub would be centred on the expansion of the Ramu nickel-cobalt operation and the construction of a refinery capable of producing nickel cathode and nickel sulphate.

“What is unique about that particular strategy in Ramu is that we are driving the expansion of Ramu from about 32,000 tonnes a year to about 74,000 tonnes of nickel produced a year,” Kanu said.

The proposed expansion, however, remains subject to regulatory approvals, agreements, financing and detailed development work.

Kanu said KMHL had acquired an interest in Ramu NiCo and was looking at acquiring a further interest in the project.

The Independent Consumer and Competition Commission announced earlier this year that it had cleared KMHL’s proposed acquisition of a 1.97 per cent participating interest in the Ramu Nickel Cobalt Joint Venture from Mineral Resources Ramu Limited.

Kanu told the conference that KMHL expected to acquire a further 20 per cent interest within the next few months, although he did not provide further details about the proposed transaction.

Ramu NiCo currently produces mixed hydroxide precipitate, or MHP, at its Basamuk processing plant.

Nickel cathode is used in manufacturing stainless steel, while nickel sulphate is an important material in battery production.

Kanu said the ultimate aim was to make nickel the first PNG base metal exported as a refined metal product.

“We want to aggregate all the nickel prospects in the country to feed into the refinery.

“We want to drive the strategy that nickel will be the first base metal that will be exported in metal cathode form. All the processing will be done in PNG.” He said.

The existing Basamuk processing plant and Kurumbukari mine could serve as foundation customers for new power developments.

Kanu said cheaper power could also help unlock the long-planned Madang Pacific Marine Industrial Zone, which would be difficult to operate competitively using diesel-generated electricity.

item.title: Hela expands water fleet to counter dry spell
item.description: The Hela provincial government has expanded its emergency drought response by purchasing four additional 10,000-liter water trucks, scheduled for delivery next month. This addition doubles the province's fleet to eight water tankers as the province copes with the intensifying El Niño drought.
item.content:encoded:
The Hela provincial government has expanded its emergency drought response by purchasing four additional 10,000-liter water trucks, scheduled for delivery next month.

This addition doubles the province's fleet to eight water tankers as the province copes with the intensifying El Niño drought.

​Hela governor Philip Undialu said the initial four trucks purchased have been operating around Tari Town, supplying water to government institutions, public servants, local churches, and nearby communities.

"With four more trucks arriving, the distribution strategy will expand across the province, allocating one water truck directly to each of the four districts to extend relief beyond the capital," he said.

​Undialu also warned customary landowners and local guardians of natural water sources to stop imposing fees or restricting public access during the severe dry spell.

​"Water is a universal human right," he said.

Undialu said anyone charging fees or blocking access during a drought could face legal consequences.

​He said natural water supplies located on private land must remain accessible to everyone in the community during this dry season.

​Governor Undialu confirmed that the Hela provincial disaster management committee has been established under National Disaster Centre’s directive.

He assured the public that the committee is working around the clock to coordinate relief efforts and safeguard communities throughout the ongoing disaster.

item.title: Starlink to boost emergency aid delivery in Milne Bay
item.description: Remote island communities and disaster officers in Milne Bay are set for faster emergency relief and real-time reporting following the delivery of new Starlink satellite communication equipment. The National Disaster Centre [NDC] provided a standard unit and a portable unit to the province on Wednesday to ensure critical communications remain online during the ongoing El Niño dry spell.
item.content:encoded:
Remote island communities and disaster officers in Milne Bay are set for faster emergency relief and real-time reporting following the delivery of new Starlink satellite communication equipment.

The National Disaster Centre [NDC] provided a standard unit and a portable unit to the province on Wednesday to ensure critical communications remain online during the ongoing El Niño dry spell.

The high-speed internet units will eliminate communication blackouts that have long delayed emergency assessments, relief supplies, and casualty updates from isolated outer islands during natural disasters.

NDC acting Director-General Lusete Laso Mana said fast, reliable communication directly impacts how quickly life-saving assistance reaches affected communities.

"El Niño is affecting many parts of the country and communication is becoming a challenge for us," Mana said.

"Some of the provinces, when contacted for reports or situational updates, do not respond promptly or do not respond at all."

He said the new satellite connection will ensure Milne Bay can transmit immediate situational reports to headquarters, allowing relief teams to deploy assistance without delay.

Milne Bay acting provincial administrator Sharon Mua said the technology brings immediate relief to provincial disaster teams who previously relied on aging VHF radio networks.

"On behalf of the provincial disaster committee and provincial government, we thank NDC for meeting our need," Mua said.

"We have been thinking of installing VHF radios because that has been working for us in the past. NDC seeing the need and bringing Starlink to our aid, we are grateful for the foresight."

The standard unit will serve as a permanent communications hub at the provincial administration office in Alotau, while the portable set will travel with emergency teams directly into disaster zones.

Milne Bay is among the first model provinces to receive the technology under an NDC initiative that will distribute 36 Starlink sets to emergency centers across the nation.

item.title: Road link to end Nomad isolation
item.description: Prime Minister James Marape has opened one of Western’s most isolated outposts, launching major infrastructure developments in Nomad, Middle Fly. Nomad Station came alive yesterday with traditional dancing and live entertainment as Marape launched the Kiunga-Nomad Road construction, breaking decades of geographical isolation by connecting the remote district directly to Kiunga’s commercial hub.
item.content:encoded:
Prime Minister James Marape has opened one of Western’s most isolated outposts, launching major infrastructure developments in Nomad, Middle Fly.

Nomad Station came alive yesterday with traditional dancing and live entertainment as Marape launched the Kiunga-Nomad Road construction, breaking decades of geographical isolation by connecting the remote district directly to Kiunga’s commercial hub.

PM Marape also launched the construction of the new Middle Fly District Administration Building and witnessed the maiden financial transaction at the newly established Nomad District Treasury Office.

The local treasury ends years of administrative delay, allowing district funds to be processed directly on site rather than through distant provincial centers.

Speaking during the historic first cheque printing, Marape urged finance officials to push towards digital operations.

"Well done. This is the first cheque to come out here, and I look forward to many more," PM said.

"More importantly, finance officials will work with the Department of Finance to migrate beyond cheques to direct electronic transactions from this station."

District leaders hailed the combined road link, administration hub, and local treasury as a major breakthrough in decentralizing government authority and bringing basic services to rural Middle Fly.

Marape was accompanied by provincial leaders and government delegates during the official launch.

item.title: Madang provincial hospital scales down services
item.description: The Madang provincial hospital will begin an indefinite scaling down of its services today due to a critical shortage of essential medical drugs and other consumables.
